category_specific_evidence: Reproducer: nansem(values, mask=mask, skipna=False, axis=0) on a 5x5 float64 array with NaN on the diagonal and one masked entry per row/column returns scalar nan instead of an array of nan (axis=1 also reproduces).
Original code: nansem had an early return 'if not skipna and mask is not None and mask.any(): return np.nan' that ignored the requested axis; the fix removes it.

Fix: when skipna=False and a mask is given, values are copied and np.putmask(values, mask, np.nan) places NaN under the mask so NaN propagates per-slice through nanvar, rather than returning a scalar.

NaN handling: masked entries must yield NaN only in the slices that contain them (test_nansem_partial_mask_no_skipna_is_per_slice asserts result[0] is nan and result[1:] are not nan with mask[0,0]=True, axis=0).
Masked extension arrays hold fill values rather than NaN underneath the mask, which is why NaN must be explicitly put under the mask for propagation.
Expected result from the issue: an array of np.nan of the same shape as the reduction output, not a scalar.
Test test_nanops_reductions_dont_skip_nan_with_mask had an xfail for nansem with skipna=False and axis in {0,1}, which was removed by the fix.
reproduction_risks: Silent on whether +/-inf, signed zero or subnormals are involved; the reproducer uses only NaN, 0.0 and finite values.
Result shape/dtype of the fixed output is not explicitly stated beyond 'array of np.nan'.
The issue reports pandas 3.1.0.dev0 with numpy 2.4.3 on Python 3.14.3; the fix's pandas version is not stated.
The reproducer prints the result rather than asserting; exact expected array shape must be inferred from the 5x5 input and axis.
